column1: # shims.tsv — the commands the operator types, and the file each one is. harbor#630.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Twenty symlinks in ~/.local/bin point into a repo that
# the harbor#619 move relocates, and NOTHING created them: each script's --help
# prints the `ln -sfn` the reader is expected to run, and the set that exists on
# this box is whatever was typed over two years. A symlink target is a literal —
# no variable, no $HOME, no expansion — so the move breaks every one of them
# loudly, and re-creating them by hand is twenty commands nobody has a list of.
# This is the list, and bin/shim-install.sh is what reads it.
# ROOT IS A VARIABLE FROM CONTRACTS/roots.tsv, never a path. That is the whole
# point: the move repoints the root in one place and every shim follows.
# THE PACKS' COMMANDS ARE NOT HERE. A workload repo's harbor-pack/ lists its own in a shims.tsv, `harbor pack install` copies it
# to <config dir>/shims.d/<repo-id>.tsv, and shim-install.sh reads both (CONTRACTS/pack.md). Core names no pack's command
# (harbor#1149), so a box with no pack links none of them.
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Shims into things harbor does not own —
# `project-init` and `projects-orchestrator` (uv tool installs, independent
# copies, they do not move), `gmail-*`/`gcal-*` (~/.local/lib/<mail tool>, which the
# runbook keeps where it is), `claude` and `python3.12` (vendor installs). And
# a BI shim that points into a workload checkout: it DOES move, and it is not
# harbor's to install. `--check` reports it as unmanaged rather than staying
# quiet, because a gate that says nothing about a thing it can see is how the
# next one gets missed.
# COLUMNS  name <TAB> root-var <TAB> path relative to that root
